record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Find a minimum-size family of negative circles whose edge sets cover all edges of a signed graph Σ.

evidence.quote: C5–8. Like C1–4, for circles that cover the edges of Σ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph $\Sigma = (G, \sigma)$ consists of an underlying graph $G = (V, E)$ together with a sign function $\sigma: E \to \{+1, -1\}$. A circle (simple cycle) $C$ in $G$ is called negative if the product $\prod_{e \in E(C)} \sigma(e) = -1$, and positive otherwise.

Given a signed graph $\Sigma$ in which every edge lies on at least one negative circle, determine (in terms of structural parameters of $\Sigma$, or via an efficient algorithm) the minimum cardinality $\mu_e^-(\Sigma)$ of a family $\mathcal{F} = \{C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_k\}$ of negative circles of $\Sigma$ such that
$$E(C_1) \cup E(C_2) \cup \cdots \cup E(C_k) = E(\Sigma),$$
i.e., every edge of $\Sigma$ is contained in the edge set of at least one circle in $\mathcal{F}$. Equivalently, find good lower and upper bounds on $\mu_e^-(\Sigma)$, and characterize the signed graphs for which such a covering family of negative circles exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of Zaslavsky's problem collection on negative circles in signed graphs. Subsequent literature (including the published version and follow-up works such as the 2024 paper on weakly negative circles versus clustering) treats these covering/packing questions as open, with no general formula or characterization for the minimum number of negative circles whose edge sets cover all edges of a signed graph.

status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work addressing related negative-circle questions in signed graphs.
